frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/my-unit/pages/MyUnitPage.tsx:45-62 — the resident-facing My Unit page imports useTranslation and uses t() for its loaded content, but its ERROR state and EMPTY state are hardcoded English literals: L49 `Could not load your unit: {error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'}` (both the prefix and the 'Unknown error' fallback are raw English), L57 `

My Unit

`, L58 `You are not currently registered as a resident of any unit.`, L59 `If you believe this is a mistake, please contact your building manager.`. A sk/cs/de resident whose unit fetch fails, or who has no unit yet, sees these screens in English only.

This is an intra-file i18n inconsistency, not a missing capability: the same component already depends on t() for the happy path (L21 `const { t } = useTranslation()`), so the error/empty branches are simply un-wrapped. Mirrors the already-tracked VotingPage/RegistryPage no-i18n class but in a DISTINCT, previously-unflagged feature dir (my-unit). Dedup: grep of all *ppt-web-ui*.json signals shows no prior my-unit finding.

Fix vector: wrap the four literals in t('myUnit.error.*' / 'myUnit.empty.*') keys and translate the 'Unknown error' fallback (reuse the shared common.unknownError key if one exists). Confidence medium: the literals are certain by static read and both branches are reachable (error = query failure, empty = resident with no unit); severity LOW (+1) as an i18n gap per the skill table.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/neighbors/pages/InvitationsPage.tsx:70-77 — formatDate calls `new Date(dateString).toLocaleDateString(undefined, { year:'numeric', month:'short', day:'numeric' })`, passing `undefined` as the locale argument. `undefined` makes the runtime fall back to the BROWSER locale, not the app's selected i18n language. In this 4-language app (sk/cs/de/en) a user who has switched the UI to Slovak but whose browser is English will see neighbor-invitation dates (sent/expiry) formatted in English, diverging from the rest of the page which is translated via t().

The repo has an established opposite convention: 12 call sites pass `i18n.language` into toLocale*String (e.g. features/disputes MediationChatThread -> formatTime(createdAt, i18n.language)). InvitationsPage ignores it. HONEST SCOPE CAVEAT: this is a widespread pattern — `grep toLocale*(undefined` returns 21 sites across features, so `undefined` is currently the majority habit; this signal flags InvitationsPage as the representative instance on a user-facing invitation list and proposes standardizing on the i18n.language convention. Previously-unflagged dir (neighbors not in the 35 flagged dirs for this class).

Fix vector: thread `const { i18n } = useTranslation()` and pass `i18n.language` as the first arg to toLocaleDateString (here and, as a follow-up sweep, at the other 20 `(undefined` sites). Confidence medium: the `undefined` locale is certain by static read; severity LOW (+1) — locale/i18n inconsistency, visible only when browser locale != selected app language.
